snippet: In his introductory remarks at the IMF Global Statistical Forum today, Klaas Knot highlighted the importance of having the right data for understanding the evolution and risks of the crypto-ecosystem.

title: You can’t always get what you want, but after 25 years of EMU, we just might find we get what we need
snippet: Not all countries benefit equally from the euro. There are three ways we can strengthen the Economic and Monetary Union and thus the euro. Klaas Knot discussed the proposals on 9 November at a seminar organised by DNB and Bruegel, a think tank.

title: ‘Challenges for monetary policy that make us think’
snippet: On 2 November Klaas Knot opened the ‘Annual Research Conference’ in Artis, Amsterdam. In his speech he said that restrictive monetary policies will likely remain needed for some time to come to get inflation back down to target.

title: Dutch pension sector’s funding ratio improves in third quarter 2023
snippet: In the third quarter of 2023, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios improve relative to the second quarter, as the decline in the value of their investments was less pronounced than the decline in the value of liabilities.

title: Confessions of a central bank cyber director
snippet: At a conference on cyber security for Chief Information Security Officers from Belgium and the Netherlands, Nicole Stolk stated that only together we can preserve people’s trust in the financial system, preserve financial stability and keep people’s data and money safe from cyberattacks.

title: Introductory remarks Klaas Knot at ECB Fifth Macroprudential Policy and Research Conference
snippet: In his introductory remarks at the Fifth Macroprudential Policy and Research Conference at the ECB in Frankfurt Klaas Knot discussed some of the challenges in using macro-prudential tools.

title: Regaining control
snippet: ‘We have made important progress in regaining control over inflation, but we are not quite there, yet. To continue this progress, and reach our target, restrictive policies will likely remain needed for some time to come. All in all, current policy is in the right place.

title: DNB imposes instruction on trust office Intertrust for incomplete procedures manual and inadequate customer due diligence
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an instruction on trust office Intertrust (Netherlands) B.V. (Intertrust) on 31 March 2022 for non-compliance with the law regarding its procedures manual and customer due diligence.

title: ‘Managing climate and environmental related risk: stepping up the pace.’
snippet: Financial institutions have to step up their efforts to adequately manage their risks related to climate change and environmental degradation. That’s what Steven Maijoor said in his key note speech at the Morningstar Sustainable Investing Summit 2023.

title: Crypto-assets regulation: from patchwork to framework
snippet: "For a long time, crypto assets were an experiment on the fringes of the financial system. [...]", said Steven Maijoor at the Digital Asset Symposium hosted jointly by the Bank of England and the Financial Stability Board on 10 October 2023.

title: Risks to financial stability increase due to rapidly rising interest rates
snippet: The Dutch financial sector must be prepared to face increasing interest rate and credit risks at financial institutions. In addition, lower liquidity in financial markets may cause price fluctuations in one market to spill over to other parts of the financial system more quickly.

title: Introductory remarks by Klaas Knot at the press conference on the FSR
snippet: “Risks to financial stability increase due to rapidly rising interest rates. Rising interest rates have made it more expensive for households and businesses in the Netherlands to borrow money.” Klaas Knot said this today at the presentation of DNB’s autumn 2023 Financial Stability Report.

title: ‘Banks going bankrupt’
snippet: At the Flairs conference Klaas Knot spoke for an audience of young bankers about the experiences with bank failures since the global financial crisis, the importance of a well functioning and credible resolution regime, and the lessons we can draw from recent cases.

title: Fine for trust office Athos Business Services (Netherlands) B.V. for insufficient customer due diligence
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €10,000 on trust office Athos Business Services (Netherlands) B.V. (Athos) on. The fine was imposed because Athos provided trust services without carrying out sufficient customer due diligence.

title: Higher export surplus boosts current account balance
snippet: The surplus on the current account of the Dutch balance of payments rose by €7.3 billion in the second quarter of 2023 (year-on-year) to €23.2 billion.

title: For how long do higher energy prices affect product prices?
snippet: Energy price hikes from 2022 still affect other prices, such as those of food. Why are some products still getting more expensive, even though energy prices have fallen again? And how long will this go on?

title: Dutch pension fund assets increasingly allocated to foreign investment funds
snippet: Dutch pension funds are increasingly investing their assets in foreign investment funds. Whereas their holdings in Dutch investment fund units have been declining for some time, an increasing share of their assets is being allocated to foreign, especially European, investment funds.

title: Peter Blom decides to step down from DNB’s Supervisory Board
snippet: Peter Blom has decided to step down as a member of DNB’s Supervisory Board. He had earlier resigned from his duties on a temporary basis on 7 November 2022. Blom has been a member of DNB's Supervisory Board since 1 September 2021.

title: Fine for trust office CIS Management for insufficient customer due diligence
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of € 156.250 on trust office CIS Management B.V. (CIS) on 25 May 2023. The fine was imposed because the customer due diligence carried out by CIS did not meet the legal requirements.

title: DNB Statistics user survey
snippet: At DNB's Statistics Division, we are constantly working to improve the quality and accessibility of our statistics. Our users expect our products and services – such as tables, statistical news releases and dashboards – to be insightful, timely and reliable.

title: Lessons from Mount Everest: acting now to curb nature-related financial risks
snippet: At the Launch Event of the NGFS Conceptual Framework on Nature-related Financial Risk Klaas Knot called for urgent action to assess and reduce the risks the nature crisis poses to the economy and the financial system.

title: Instruction imposed on CCV Group B.V. for non-compliance with Wwft
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an instruction on CCV Group B.V. (CCV) on 13 March 2019 because CCV had failed to comply with certain provisions of the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Act (Wet ter voorkoming van witwassen en financieren van terrorisme – Wwft).

title: 1.8 million Dutch households would rather be in a different housing situation
snippet: Buy or rent? The housing situation of 1.8 million households in the Netherlands does not match their preferences. This means they currently rent their home but would prefer to buy, or own a home but would prefer to rent.

title: Else Bos to step down as Executive Board Member and Chair of Prudential Supervision of DNB
snippet: In early 2024, Else Bos will step down as member of the Executive Board and Chair of Prudential Supervision of DNB.

title: The Netherlands European leader in green bonds
snippet: Dutch companies have once again raised more capital by issuing green bonds, new figures from DNB reveal. In relative terms, the Netherlands is the leader in the euro area when it comes to issuing green debt securities.

title: Instruction for de Volksbank for deficient assessment of money laundering and terrorist financing risks
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) issued an instruction on de Volksbank N.V (Volksbank) on 12 June 2023 because de Volksbank was gravely deficient in its statutory obligation to identify, analyse and assess its money laundering and terrorist financing risks.

title: DNB Statistics user survey
snippet: At DNB's Statistics Division, we are constantly working to improve the quality and accessibility of our statistics. Our users expect our products and services – such as tables, statistical news releases and dashboards – to be insightful, timely and reliable.

title: DNB signs agreements with TCS and Capgemini for IT services
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) has signed four-year agreements with TCS and Capgemini for the provision of IT services. From 2024, these companies will support the central bank as it accelerates its digital ambitions.

title: Artie Debidien appointed to DNB Supervisory Board from 1 September
snippet: On the recommendation of DNB’s Supervisory Board, Dutch Finance Minister Sigrid Kaag has decided to appoint Artie Debidien on behalf of the shareholder. She will succeed Margot Scheltema, who will step down after her term ends on 1 September 2023.

title: Dutch household portfolio investments rise in value again
snippet: The value of portfolio investments held by Dutch households continued to increase in the second quarter of 2023. The total value of portfolio investments at the end of June was €165.9 billion, an increase of €5.1 billion (+3.2%) compared to the previous quarter.

title: Falling energy prices mask high Dutch core inflation
snippet: The recent drop in energy prices pushed Dutch inflation down to the European average of 5.3% in July. However, core inflation (HICP excluding energy and food) remains higher in the Netherlands than in the euro area. One possible explanation is the more pronounced overheating of the Dutch economy.

title: "With our own transition plan, we aim to make a positive contribution to sustainability."
snippet: DNB has updated its sustainable finance strategy. It addresses climate-related and environmental risks for the economy and the financial sector, climate-proofing the Netherlands and social issues. Also, DNB gradually raises the bar on sustainability in its supervision of financial institutions.

title: Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds opens DNB Fund
snippet: The DNB Fund is open as from Friday, 30 June, 10:00. This means you can submit your funding proposal through the Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds website.

title: “High hopes: rooting the CMU in sustainable finance”
snippet: “Currently, the European economy has a large dependency on the banking system. But this banking-bias makes us vulnerable. It increases systemic risk, and as a result, it decreases our resilience to financial shocks.

title: Cash plays an important role for different groups in Dutch society
snippet: People with disabilities or low digital literacy or who have difficulty making ends meet particularly value cash. Of all Dutch people, 28% say they cannot do without cash and 7% say they only pay with cash at points of sale, but these percentages are higher for the aforementioned focus groups.

title: Netherlands' current account surplus revised upwards
snippet: The current account surplus of the Dutch balance of payments was higher in 2021 and 2022 than previously recorded. This is mainly due to higher adjusted profits of listed multinationals and larger exports than previously projected.

title: Fine for trust office Lewben Netherlands B.V. for failing to commission audits
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed a fine of €10,000 on trust office Lewben Netherlands B.V. (Lewben) on 19 January 2023. The fine was imposed for Lewben's failure to commission audits during the period from 1 January 2019 to 7 September 2021.

title: Economic growth slows, inflation remains persistent
snippet: The Dutch economy will grow by 0.8% this year, which is sharply lower than last year's 4.5% growth. While inflation is set to decrease, in part due to the economy cooling down, it remains too high at 4.2%.

title: Fine for trust office TMF Netherlands B.V. for insufficient customer due diligence
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €3,125,000 on trust office TMF Netherlands B.V. (TMF) on 2 March 2023. The fine was imposed because the customer due diligence carried out by TMF did not meet the legal requirements. *Adjusted on 20 February 2026

title: Netherlands suffered income loss in 2022 from higher energy prices
snippet: Partly due to sharply higher energy prices in 2021 and 2022, the Netherlands had to pay more to foreign countries to import the same amount of goods and services.

title: Dutch pension funds invest more in the Netherlands
snippet: Following four quarters of declining assets, the assets under management of Dutch pension funds increased again in the first quarter of 2023. This increase can mainly be ascribed to price gains, especially of equities.

title: "Keeping our windshiels intact: lessons from the recent market turmoil"
snippet: In Europe, we have implemented the Basel standards more consistently across banks of all sizes. But let's not forget that the Basel III standards have not yet been fully implemented in European regulation.

title: Introductory line for the Standing Parliamentary Committee for Finance
snippet: “Dutch banks have so far remained in good shape, and that is borne out by a stress test that we conducted. Banks can certainly withstand stress. But we cannot sit back and assume that the worst is over.”

title: “Bold, but realistic: monetary policy and financial stability”
snippet: In his keynote speech at the 5th Capital Markets Seminar, jointly organized by the European Stability Mechanism, the European Investment Bank and the European Commission, Klaas Knot discussed the current state of economic and financial affairs.

title: “To improve is to change”
snippet: On 1 June, Klaas Knot gave a speech at the International Banking Summit in Brussels. He stated that “our financial system has to be able to absorb change, to withstand shocks and address vulnerabilities. In other words: the global financial system has to be resilient.

title: Rapid rise in interest rates exposes financial vulnerabilities
snippet: Persistently high inflation and rising interest rates are making the risks to financial stability both tangible and visible, as can be seen from the recent failure of a number of regional banks in the United States.

title: Minister takes initiative to preserve cash
snippet: Finance Minister Sigrid Kaag wants banks to continue to provide adequate, basic cash facilities, as she wrote today in a letter to Parliament. In her letter, she also stresses that cash withdrawals and deposits must remain affordable for both consumers and retailers.

title: Incentives for people to work more (or fewer) hours
snippet: One in three working people in the Netherlands is prepared to work more hours if it means a higher salary. People would also be willing to work more hours if their work were more fun, if remote working were easier and if they could spend less time caring for their children.

title: Low income and job insecurity often occur in combination with other vulnerabilities
snippet: People with low incomes and insecure jobs are also more likely to be vulnerable in other areas, such as their housing situation and asset position. About a quarter of this group seems unable to escape their vulnerable position.

title: Dutch households book investment gains in first quarter of 2023
snippet: Dutch investors started off well in 2023 – in the first quarter, the value of investments held by Dutch households increased by €7.8 billion. Despite the turmoil in financial markets, Dutch households also invested more in equities and bonds issued by banks.

title: DNB and Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds: new fund for historical links to slavery
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), together with the Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds (Culture Fund), is setting up a special fund to help address the impact of nineteenth-century transatlantic slavery.

title: ECB interest rate hikes have a higher pass-through to mortgage than to savings rates
snippet: While interest rates on mortgages have risen sharply following the ECB's recent rate hikes, the increase of interest rates on savings accounts has been limited so far. Banks do not pass on an ECB rate hike equally to their customers as they wish to maintain their interest margin.

title: Fine for IJmond Corporate Solutions B.V. for not having two directors in time
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €47,500 on IJmond Corporate Solutions B.V. (IJCS) on 4 February 2020. The administrative fine is imposed because IJCS did not have two directors from 1 July 2019 until at least 19 August 2019.

title: Will Dutch first-time buyers be able to afford a home again?
snippet: From the autumn of 2023, first-time buyers will find homes slightly more affordable. Although house prices are falling, first-time buyers’ mortgage costs are higher than a year ago as mortgage rates have gone up.

title: Public trust in financial institutions remains stable despite turmoil in financial markets
snippet: Dutch households' trust in financial institutions has remained stable over the past year, despite the recent problems faced by banks in the United States and Switzerland. During that period, households did think slightly more often about the possibility of Dutch banks failing.

title: More banks see drop in demand for residential mortgage loans
snippet: An increasing number of banks are reporting a drop in demand for residential mortgage loans, as revealed in the latest Bank Lending Survey.

title: Card payments up in 2022
snippet: Dutch consumers and businesses made around 6.1 billion payments using a debit or credit card in 2022, representing a combined amount of €182 billion, new figures from DNB on payment transactions show.

title: Speech Klaas Knot – “Mamma Mia, Here We Go Again? Lessons from SVB and Credit Suisse”
snippet: “So far, no shock has been the Waterloo of our global financial system. But we need to remain vigilant. We need to remain diligent, in mapping, measuring, and monitoring vulnerabilities. Old and new.” This is what Klaas Knot said at Eurofi’s High Level Seminar 2023 in Stockholm.

title: Dutch pension sector’s funding ratio improves
snippet: In the first quarter of 2023, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios improve relative to the previous quarter, as growth in their investments outstripped the increase in liabilities.

title: Dutch people are attached to their cash
snippet: More than 90% of Dutch people think it is important to be able to pay with cash. They find the €20 banknote the most beautiful, and more than two-thirds of respondents said they had never held a banknote in their hands that they doubted was genuine.

title: Many Dutch are doing well, but for some, vulnerabilities are accumulating
snippet: If Dutch households are vulnerable, they are often vulnerable in several areas at once. For instance, households with high housing expenses relative to income are also more likely than average to have a poor position in the labour market and limited financial buffers, according to a new study by DNB

title: Speech Klaas Knot – The Whitaker lecture - ‘Striving for financial stability’
snippet: On 19 April Klaas Knot gave the annual Whitaker Lecture in Dublin where he made clear that “to maintain financial stability we do not only have to adapt to changing conditions, we also have to create the conditions to be able to adapt when stability is threatened.

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - “Paying attention – on the supervision of payment institutions"
snippet: “The thriving payments industry in our country is reflected in the enthusiastic use of your services by tonnes of Dutch businesses and organisations.

title: Rise of BigTechs requires adjustments in financial supervision
snippet: The rising importance of BigTechs such as Google, Amazon, Apple and Facebook in the financial sector requires special attention from supervisory authorities such as De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: Paying with mobile as popular as cash at checkout
snippet: In 2022, Dutch people used their mobile phone or wearable device for contactless payment at points of sale as often as they paid in cash. The share of these new means of payment rose to 21%, while the use of banknotes and coins stabilised at 20% of total payments.

title: New climate and environmental risk management guide for the financial sector
snippet: Climate change and environmental degradation can result in direct and indirect damage, including financial damage. This means they impact the work of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: Bond financing less popular among mortgage lenders
snippet: Mortgage lenders are financing Dutch residential mortgages less and less often by selling bonds with these mortgages as collateral, new figures from DNB reveal.

title: Martin van Rijn appointed Chair of DNB's Supervisory Board from 1 June 2023
snippet: On the recommendation of the Supervisory Board (SB) of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), Finance Minister Sigrid Kaag, on behalf of DNB’s shareholder, the Dutch State, has decided to appoint Martin van Rijn as Chair of the SB.

title: Trust office licence of D-Max Corporate B.V. revoked
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) revoked the trust office licence of D-Max Corporate B.V. (D-Max) on 21 October 2022. DNB revoked the trust office licence of D-Max for two reasons.

title: Current account surplus dips below 6% standard
snippet: At 5.6%, the Dutch current account surplus as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP), based on three-year averages, was below the European Commission's 6% standard in 2022 for the first time in more than a decade, as revealed by new DNB figures.

title: Introduction, DNB Annual Report 2022 press conference
snippet: “Despite the shocks of recent years, the Dutch economy and the Dutch financial sector are in good shape.” Klaas Knot said this today at the presentation of DNB’s 2022 Annual Report. He reflected on the events of 2022 and looked ahead to the economic challenges facing us down the road.

title: Challenges for our economy in 2023
snippet: 2022 was a turbulent year, with major events worldwide that affected nearly all of us to a greater of lesser extent. This year too, we see the impact of these events clearly reflected in our economy. We outline the most important below, but first we take a brief look back at 2022.

title: Who is responsible for fighting inflation?
snippet: Central banks were created specifically to ensure stable prices and intervene when needed. Why do we need price stability, and why do many people think this is the government’s responsibility?

title: Pension funds suffer losses on real estate
snippet: After years of price gains, pension funds suffered losses on their real estate investments in 2022, DNB figures show. Overall, the value of these investments fell by over €14 billion. Listed real estate in particular fell in value, while losses in directly held properties were limited.

title: DNB imposes order subject to penalty on an enterprise for failing to provide information
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank N.V. (DNB) has imposed an order subject to penalty on the enterprise because the enterprise failed to cooperate with DNB’s request for information in a timely manner.

title: How inflation reached all-time highs in two years
snippet: For years, inflation in the euro area hovered around 1.5%, below the European Central Bank's (ECB) target of around 2%, despite historically low interest rates. But then it suddenly shot up in summer 2021, peaking at 10.6% in October 2022. How could inflation go up so fast?

title: Dutch households invest more in emerging markets
snippet: In 2022, Dutch households again invested more in emerging markets such as South Africa, Brazil and China. Despite net purchases, the value of these investments decreased to €2,241 million at the end of 2022 due to price losses, down from a record €2,631 million at the end of 2021.

title: Timely and consistent implementation of Basel III important for European banks
snippet: Global agreements on strengthening banks’ capital positions, as contained in the Basel III Accord, should be implemented in Europe as rapidly and consistently as possible.

title: Some retail sectors refuse cash payments too often
snippet: What is the state of cash acceptance in shops and by other retailers in the Netherlands? DNB monitors developments annually.

title: Target sustainability measures at financially vulnerable households
snippet: In response to soaring energy prices, the vast majority of Dutch households have turned down the thermostat and started taking shorter or fewer showers.

title: Fine for Travelex for failing to report unusual transactions in time
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €100,000 on Travelex N.V. (Travelex; formerly: Grenswisselkantoor – GWK) on 2 February 2023. T

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Staying the course”
snippet: Speaking on 8 February 2023, Klaas Knot discussed recent inflation developments and how they affect the ECB's monetary policy.

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - “The human life of cyber resilience”
snippet: “It is hard to predict when or where the next cyberattack will hit, but chances are that it will have to do with a human error. So it is important that people, in all layers of an organisation, know the why of it all. Why they need to follow certain processes and procedures. Why they need to...

title: Speech Klaas Knot - ‘What can central banks do to help save our planet?
snippet: In his opening speech for the Climate Risk Conference in Slovakia on 7 February 2023, Klaas Knot said that central banks are not in the driving seat to save our planet but are definitely part of the team: “A part of the team in three different ways, in three different roles."

title: Trust in central bank and national politics has fallen due to high inflation
snippet: The Dutch population's trust in De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) and national politics has fallen. This is partly caused by the unprecedented high inflation over the past year.

title: Dutch pension sector funding ratio down, mainly due to indexation
snippet: In the fourth quarter of 2022, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios deteriorate relative to the third quarter, as the value of liabilities increased, while pension assets remained almost unchanged.

title: Increase in counterfeit euro banknotes of very low quality
snippet: More counterfeit euro banknotes were withdrawn from circulation in the Netherlands in 2022 than in the previous year. A total of 38,200 were found, 47% more than in 2021. This increase is mainly due to a limited number of fraud cases involving counterfeit euro banknotes of very low quality.

title: Digital banking is a struggle for many
snippet: Some 2.6 million Dutch people aged 18 and above struggle with their digital payments and other banking affairs. This has emerged from a study conducted by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: Millions of Dutch struggle to get to grips with digital payments
snippet: 2.6 million Dutch adults do not manage all their banking affairs on their own. This has emerged from a study conducted by DNB. Although many of them would like to be more self-reliant, they need assistance for a variety of reasons.

title: Dutch households continue saving steadily even post-pandemic
snippet: In 2022, bank balances of Dutch households increased further. The aggregate balance held in payment and savings accounts rose by €34.1 billion last year to reach €562.5 billion (equal to 61% of annual GDP). Dutch people continued to put aside substantial amounts in 2022, DNB statistics show.

title: DNB imposes administrative fine on Coinbase Europe Limited for providing crypto services without the legally required registration until 22 September 2022
snippet: On 18 January 2023, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €3,325,000 on Coinbase Europe Limited (Coinbase). The fine was imposed because Coinbase provided crypto services in the Netherlands in the past without registration with DNB, which is in non-compliance with the law.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - 'Daring to know in times of uncertainty and structural shifts'
snippet: "Dare to know," said Klaas Knot at the ILF conference on systemic risks, relating the Financial Stability Board’s (FSB) role of enhancing the resilience of the global financial system to the Enlightenment adage of "sapere aude”.

title: Five questions on our new sustainability figures
snippet: DNB, together with the ECB and other central banks, is publishing new sustainability figures for the financial sector this week. Why, in fact? And what exactly are we measuring? See the Q&As below.

title: Smaller carbon footprint from large investors’ equity portfolios
snippet: The equity portfolios of Dutch pension funds and insurers have become significantly “greener” over the 2017-2020 period. This is mainly because investee companies have emitted less carbon over that period, according to an analysis by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: Interview Klaas Knot in La Stampa
snippet: Interview with Klaas Knot by Marco Zatterin and Fabrizio Goria of La Stampa. The interview was published on January 21, 2023.

title: Interview Klaas Knot in the Financial Times
snippet: Interview with Klaas Knot by Martin Arnold of the Financial Times. Published on December 26, 2022.

title: Current account balance in line with last year
snippet: The Dutch current account balance of €13.9 billion (6% of GDP based on three-year averages) in the third quarter of 2022 was €0.3 billion lower than a year earlier, according to figures from DNB.

title: Exchanging Croatian banknotes at DNB
snippet: You can temporarily exchange Croatian banknotes for euros at DNB. The reason is the introduction of the euro in Croatia. The exchange rate: 7.53450 kuna = 1 euro.

title: Banks at risk due to slow pace of climate transition by companies
snippet: Companies in carbon-intensive sectors to which banks lend are not switching to sustainable alternatives quickly enough to meet the goals of the Paris Climate Agreement. This has emerged from an analysis conducted by DNB.

title: Use of cash lower in euro area countries
snippet: In most euro area countries, cash is used less and less in point-of-sale (POS) payments, whereas debit and credit cards are used more and more frequently. Nevertheless, cash remains the most important means of payment for six in ten people in the euro area.

title: Dutch economy cools due to high inflation and lower global trade
snippet: The Dutch economy has been cooling since the middle of 2022 and will stabilise at 0.8% gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 2023. This cooling is caused by high inflation and slowing world trade growth.

title: Inflation reduced faster if central bank and governments apply brakes simultaneously
snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) can bring down high inflation by tightening its monetary policy. This can be achieved more quickly if fiscal policy is also restrictive. This is shown in a new study by economists from DNB and Radboud University.

title: Warning against MEK Global Limited, doing business as ‘KuCoin’
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) announces that MEK Global Limited (MGL), doing business as ‘KuCoin’, is providing crypto services in the Netherlands without the required legal registration with DNB.

title: Unveiling of art installation on Frederiksplein
snippet: On Friday 2 July, DNB President Klaas Knot unveiled an art installation on the Frederiksplein square, together with local residents.

title: Adequate pricing of biodiversity risks requires higher-quality data
snippet: The financial sector is exposed to risks as a result of biodiversity loss. To manage these risks adequately, the quality of available biodiversity data must be improved. For this reason, DNB is urging for creation of more transparent and standardised biodiversity indicators at the COP15 conference.

title: Less non-bank financing in the Netherlands in 2021
snippet: Dutch non-bank financial services providers provided €401 billion in financing in 2021, 14% less than in 2020. This left the sector as large as one-sixth of the Dutch banking system, accounting for 1% of global non-bank financing.

title: Effective from 1 January 2023, Frans Muller has been appointed to the Supervisory Board of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB)
snippet: On the recommendation of DNB’s Supervisory Board (SB), Dutch Finance Minister Sigrid Kaag has decided to appoint Frans Muller on behalf of the shareholder. He will succeed Feike Sijbesma, who will step down at the General Meeting on 22 March 2023, after ten years.

title: Dutch insurers are selling many assets this year
snippet: Dutch insurers sold €23 billion worth of assets on balance so far this year, DNB figures show. They used about three quarters of the proceeds to meet the margin requirements under derivatives contracts. I

title: Chip manufacturers largest among Dutch listed companies
snippet: Companies in the chip industry account for almost a quarter of the market capitalisation of all listed companies having their registered office in the Netherlands, a DNB analysis shows.

title: Dutch households suffer large losses on investment fund positions
snippet: Dutch households suffered large losses on investment funds in the first three quarters of 2022, DNB figures show. Falling stock market prices and rising interest rates reduced the size of investments in funds by €18.3 billion (-15.9%) to €97.3 billion in the first nine months of this year.

title: Renters in social housing are less likely to move
snippet: Renters in the private sector are on average 2.5 times more likely to move to a different region than homeowners. Renters in the social sector, on the other hand, are 1.4 times more likely to move than homeowners. This is the result of recent DNB research.

title: Klaas Knot speaks with MPs about inflation
snippet: What has caused the recent sharp rise in inflation, and where is it heading? And what is the European Central Bank doing to bring inflation back to the 2% target? DNB President Klaas Knot answered these and other questions in a meeting with a parliamentary committee on Thursday afternoon.

title: Variable and short-term mortgage rates increasingly popular
snippet: Dutch households are increasingly taking out variable-rate mortgage loans or fixed-rate residential mortgage loans of up to one year, DNB data show.

title: Blog Inge van Dijk - Preparing the euro for a digital future
snippet: The digital euro has been in the news more and more lately. And rightly so, as digital payments are on the rise. But what is the digital euro, and why is it being developed? Inge van Dijk, DNB's director of Payments, explains.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - In resolute pursuit of price stability
snippet: “For a long time, inflation was hardly on anyone’s mind. But today, it has become a key issue for everyone.” In his keynote address at the 32nd Frankfurt European Banking Congress, Klaas Knot spoke about the ECB’s resolute pursuit of price stability.

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - Public trust: the litmus test of financial innovation
snippet: “Adequate regulation and supervision of governance, risk management, and transparency are quintessential elements of a well-functioning financial system that passes the litmus test of the public’s trust.

title: Trust in DNB benefits from greater awareness of the financial supervisor's tasks and responsibilities
snippet: On average, the Dutch public has fairly high trust in De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) as the supervisory authority for financial institutions. DNB's execution of the Dutch Deposit Guarantee, which insures account holders' balances up to €100,000, contributes greatly to this level of trust.

title: Insurers in the Netherlands must respond to new and changing risks
snippet: Dutch households and businesses have very limited insurance cover against new and changing risks, such as those from floods and cyberattacks. Responding to this situation offers Dutch insurers opportunities to continue fulfilling their role in society and strengthen their future resilience.

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - Into the unknown: decision-making in uncertain times
Inflation can affect banks in many different ways
snippet: In many respects, Dutch banks are in a very different position when dealing with the impact of high inflation than they were in the 1970s and 1980s, when consumer prices also rose rapidly.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - 25th Annual DNB Research Conference
'We do not see cryptos as money'
snippet: DNB experts Vera Lubbersen and Peter Wierts took a close look at all the developments in crypto assets. An interview on the pros and cons, how cryptos fit in our money system, and what new regulations will mean for crypto providers.

title: Proper regulation indispensable for risky cryptos
snippet: It is of the utmost importance that rules are swiftly agreed upon internationally to regulate the use of crypto-assets such as Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether.

title: Unbacked crypto-assets not suitable as money
snippet: Unbacked crypto-assets like Bitcoin are mainly used as speculative and risky investments, and their value is highly volatile. Bitcoin is therefore ill-suited as a means of payment, store of value or unit of account, and this means it is unsuitable as money.

title: Peter Blom to temporarily step down as DNB Supervisory Board member
snippet: Peter Blom has decided to temporarily step down as a member of the Supervisory Board of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) with effect from 7 November 2022.

title: Avoiding a wage-price spiral requires effort from governments, central banks and social partners
snippet: Faced with soaring inflation that is eroding purchasing power, workers will try to compensate by negotiating higher wages. As the resulting pressure on profit margins grows, employers will in turn try to pass on higher wages in the prices they charge their customers.

title: Non-financial companies lead in green bonds
snippet: Dutch companies are increasingly raising capital by issuing green bonds, new figures from DNB reveal.

title: Slow growth in corporate lending before the pandemic mainly due to low demand
snippet: A recent DNB analysis finds that the main driver behind the pre-pandemic sluggish corporate credit growth has been subdued demand. It also suggests that corporate bank lending in the Netherlands decreases more after a crisis and takes longer to recover compared to the rest of the euro area.

title: Dutch pension sector’s funding ratio improves
snippet: In the third quarter of 2022, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios improve relative to the second quarter, as the value of their liabilities showed a steeper decline than their assets.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Policy Responses in a Pandemic- and Conflict-Impacted World”
snippet: Introduction Klaas Knot delivered at the G30 panel

title: A feasible and affordable insurance guarantee scheme for policyholders
snippet: An insurance guarantee scheme (IGS) can be designed such that it offers policyholders affordable additional protection for their insurance. This emerged from a study conducted by De Nederlandsche Bank into the feasibility and affordability of such a scheme in the Netherlands.

title: Three takeaways from our biodiversity conference
snippet: DNB and the OMFIF Sustainable Policy Institute have hosted a one-day conference on the relevance of biodiversity loss for the financial system and vice versa, and on the role of public and private finance in the preservation of biodiversity.

title: Introductory remarks by Klaas Knot at the press conference on the FSR
snippet: Good morning everyone and a warm welcome to this press conference on the Financial Stability Report. I would like to start with a brief outline of the key messages from the FSR and I will then be happy to answer your questions.

title: Inflation and growth outlook put financial sector to the test
snippet: Financial stability risks have increased over the past six months. High inflation, rising interest rates, the war in Ukraine and the possibility of a global recession have combined to create an unprecedented situation.

title: MiCAR important step in regulation of crypto markets
snippet: The new EU regulation for issuers of crypto assets and crypto service providers – the Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation (MiCAR) – is a welcome step in the regulation of European crypto markets, according to DNB in response to the recent agreement reached in Brussels on the regulation.

title: The Sustainable Finance Platform launches e-learning biodiversity basics for professionals of financial institutions
snippet: Ben jij een professional bij een financiële instelling en wil je in minder dan een uur meer leren over biodiversiteit? Dan is deze nieuwe e-learning die je de basisbeginselen over biodiversiteit bijbrengt iets voor jou.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - To quagga or not to quagga? Time to restore the balance
snippet: During the DNB - OMFIF conference at Artis Klaas Knot called out for action to prevent biodiversity loss: “Our demand for nature’s goods and services far exceeds our planet’s ability to produce them on a sustainable basis. Now it’s time to restore the balance and save our planet and our economy.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Navigating climate-related financial risks”
snippet: “There is no GPS to navigate climate-related risks. The navigation tools are still being developed. But fortunately, progress is being achieved rapidly – and it is up to us to catch the wind in our sails. The FSB Roadmap is an important tool to help us do that.”

title: Speech Klaas Knot - Working on progress. On public and private risk sharing in the EMU
snippet: “We have thirty years of experience to learn from. Thirty years of crises and successes, of design flaws and great innovation, of opportunities for reform that we have missed, and opportunities for prosperity gains that we have seized.” This is what Klaas Knot said at the Maastricht Treaty.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Spreading our wings. How monetary and fiscal policy can fight inflation”
snippet: “The job for central bankers is clear. Like on the painting, we will rise up, fiercely spread our wings, and protect our eggs from the menacing mongrel of inflation,” said Klaas Knot, referring to "The Threatened Swan" at the informal dinner of the Economic and Financial Committee at the Rijksmuseum

title: Current account surplus revised sharply downwards
snippet: The Dutch current account balance has been revised downwards for the period 2015-2021 following recent research by Statistics Netherlands.

title: Households again suffer big losses on equities
snippet: Dutch households again lost a significant amount of wealth in the stock market in the second quarter of 2022.

title: DNB foresees deterioration of capital position
snippet: The European Central Bank is tightening monetary policy in response to high inflation. This will have a negative impact on the profitability of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) and therefore on its capital position, as DNB has disclosed in a letter to Finance Minister Sigrid Kaag.

title: Data Mobility and the Financial Sector: How to Regulate?
snippet: Data and data mobility are having a growing impact on financial services. Moreover, new EU regulation has been proposed or is expected that aims to create an EU data market by 2030 by enhancing the ability of data holders to share their data.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Towards a sustainable economy”
snippet: “Sustainable finance is not only about managing financial risks, about stability. Sustainability is also about change. About making better choices for a better world.” That was the message of Klaas Knot in his lecture at One Planet, where he spoke to an audience of mainly students.

title: Speech Olaf Sleijpen - “Embracing a healthy economy”
snippet: Since 2011, the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences and De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) together facilitate the Annual Inspire2Live Congress. In this year’s edition, executive board member of DNB Olaf Sleijpen held a speech.

title: Dutch current account surplus back at 2019 level
snippet: In the fourth quarter of 2021, the surplus on the Dutch current account amounted to €15.2 billion, bringing the full-2021 surplus to €81.4 billion.

title: Fight against money laundering must be more focused
snippet: A more risk-based approach will sharpen the focus of efforts to keep the financial sector free from financial crime.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “From thaler to tackle. On how to lift us out of the current crises”
snippet: “The early days of the pandemic serve as a stark reminder that - in our globalized economies - inward-looking policies almost always lead to a negative sum game.

title: Biggest money laundering risks must be given top priority
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank has published a report on preventing and combating financial crime. It recommends zooming in on the high-risk customer categories. An interview with Loes Wenink, supervisor at DNB.

title: Dutch pension funds sell record amount in assets
snippet: Dutch pension funds sold €88 billion worth of assets in the first half of 2022, according to figures from DNB. They used part of the proceeds to meet the margin requirements under derivatives contracts, which had risen due to increased interest rates.

title: “A time to act. The outlook for monetary policy in the euro area.”
snippet: "The current environment implies that the path and endpoint of the policy rate will be uncertain. That also implies that we will continue to take our decisions on a meeting-by-meeting basis, and that we will persevere until the inflation outlook has stabilized,” said Klaas Knot...

title: Workers with no occupational pension also save little privately
snippet: A substantial part of the Dutch working population does not participate in an occupational pension scheme. A significant part of this group does not compensate for this with other forms of savings either.

title: ECB monetary toolkit constantly evolving
snippet: In the aftermath of the Global Financial Crisis, central banks vastly expanded their toolkits in order to continue fulfilling their mandate. In addition to the regular rate setting policy, they have added new instruments such as asset purchase programmes and targeted lending operations to banks.

title: Wages are rising in line with inflation to a limited extent
snippet: There are currently no indications that inflation, through wage increases and a self-reinforcing wage-price spiral, will develop into long-term high inflation. This means there is room for more wage growth in the current macroeconomic conditions.

title: Inflation is high, but context differs from the 1970s
snippet: The current high inflation in the Netherlands occurs in a different economic environment than in the 1970s. Back then, the labour market, the financial position of businesses and monetary policy were a breeding ground for stagflation.

title: Dutch pension funds’ average funding ratio improved
snippet: In the second quarter of 2022, Dutch pension funds saw their average funding ratio improve relative to the first quarter, as the value of their liabilities showed a steeper decline than their assets. Pension assets went down by €190 billion to €1,517 billion.

title: ECB announces new instrument in fight against rising inflation
snippet: On Thursday, 21 July the European Central Bank (ECB), in addition to a 0.5% interest rate increase, announced the transmission protection instrument (TPI).

title: Higher energy costs have limited impact on corporate profits
snippet: At a macro level, the sharp increase in energy prices has a limited impact on the profitability of Dutch companies. Even in an extreme scenario, the negative consequences remain manageable.

title: Trust in financial institutions stable
snippet: Public trust in financial institutions has remained stable over the past year, while trust in other sectors (such as politics and the public sector) has decreased. This has emerged from a DNB survey held among more than 2,200 Dutch households.

title: Russian invasion contributes to fall in Dutch current account balance
snippet: The Dutch current account balance of €20.2 billion in the first quarter of 2022 was €2.3 billion lower than a year earlier, according to figures from DNB. This was due to lower revenues from abroad, including Russia.

title: DNB apologises for its historical links to slavery
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) apologises for its role in the Atlantic trade in enslaved people in the nineteenth century. DNB is also taking measures to help reduce the repercussions of the legacy of slavery for those directly affected to this day.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Keti Koti 2022 marks turning point for DNB”
snippet: “Today, on behalf of De Nederlandsche Bank, I apologise. I offer our sincere apologies to all descendants of enslaved people in the Netherlands, in Suriname, in Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, in Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten.

title: Income flowing to tax havens through the Netherlands significantly down
snippet: Income from foreign direct investment (FDI) in the Netherlands flowing to low-tax countries has fallen sharply over the past two years. This is probably due to newly introduced national and international legislation, according to a DNB analysis.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Macroprudential supervision: what’s in a name?”
snippet: “The current macroprudential framework is not yet complete and effective to address all the different systemic risks within the financial system.

title: War in Ukraine hits newly recovered Dutch economy
snippet: The Dutch economy has shown a rapid and strong recovery following the coronavirus (COVID-19) recession. The Russian aggression against Ukraine is driving energy prices higher amid greater uncertainty, and global trade is under pressure.

title: Cyber risks also relevant to financial stability
snippet: With the ongoing digitalisation of financial services, cyber threats are posing increasing risks for the financial sector. In a new study, DNB investigates under which circumstances a cyber incident at a financial institution could develop into a threat for the financial system as a whole.

title: Regenerative finance solutions to restore and conserve biodiversity
snippet: The Biodiversity Working Group of the Sustainable Finance Platform, together with the Erasmus Platform for Sustainable Value Creation, today published its study “Financing regenerative agriculture”.

title: Dutch households suffered large losses from equity investments in first quarter of 2022
snippet: The volume of investments by Dutch households in listed equities fell by €3.0 billion to €58.9 billion in the first quarter of 2022. The 4.9% drop compared to the previous quarter was mainly due to falling share prices; only a small part was caused by sales of shares.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Propelling a graceful transition: the role of the financial system”
snippet: For his speech at the Green Swan Conference, Klaas Knot spoke in his capacity as Chair of the Financial Stability Board (FSB) about the role of the financial sector in the transition to net-zero.

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - “Data make the world go round: on open data and open finance”
snippet: “Data are essential to innovate financial products and financial processes. To enable financial institutions to offer cheaper, faster and more personalised services. To increase efficiency and economic growth,” Steven Maijoor said at the 6th edition of FinTech meets the Regulators.

title: Klaas Knot’s introductory statement
snippet: “Last year, we focused on the impact of the COVID-19 crisis. Just when we seem to have put the COVID-19 pandemic behind us and embarked on a strong economic recovery, the economy and the financial system are being tested again.”

title: DNB activates countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB) in the Netherlands
snippet: We have increased the countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB) from 0% to 1%. As a result, banks that provide loans in the Netherlands – including banks from outside the Netherlands – must set aside extra capital for these loans. For the Dutch banking sector as a whole this amounts to an...

title: 95% of guaranteed savings deposits of bankrupt ATB now paid out
snippet: One month after the bankruptcy of Amsterdam Trade Bank (ATB), 95% of the guaranteed savings deposits have already been paid to ATB’s duped account holders. About 80% of all customers have applied for compensation.

title: Financial stability risks increased due to war and high inflation
snippet: After a strong recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, the war in Ukraine and high inflation have worsened the economic outlook and increased financial stability risks. In addition to the enormous humanitarian consequences in Ukraine itself, the economic and financial impact of the war...

title: How does DNB's profit and loss account work?
snippet: Commercial banks end the year on a profit or loss, but what about a central bank like De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB)? And what happens if DNB makes a profit, or indeed a loss? Does DNB maintain buffers to absorb losses? And what’s the financial bottom line after 23 years of working with the euro?

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - Data Science for Supervision: What’s in it for us?
snippet: How can supervisors leverage data even better in supervision? This is the key question in Steven Maijoor’s speech at the Data Science Conference of the DNB Data Science Hub.

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - “On how climate-related and environmental risks affect banking and its prudential supervision”
snippet: On 11 May, Steven Maijoor spoke at the AFME European Sustainable Finance conference. He talked about how climate-related and environmental (C&E) risks affect the financial system and about how supervisors and banks must respond to these risks.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - Diverse challenges, common threads: Preserving global financial stability today and tomorrow
snippet: On May 11, Klaas Knot spoke at the International Swaps and Derivatives Association in Madrid in his capacity as chairman of the Financial Stability Board (FSB). He talked about the current challenges to global financial stability and the measures being taken by the FSB to address them.

title: Dutch institutional investors increasingly turn to high-risk bonds
snippet: In the past two years, Dutch institutional investors increasingly preferred riskier high-yield (HY) bonds over their safer investment-grade (IG) counterparts. Most of these investments in HY debt securities are made abroad, for example in US firms and Brazilian and South African governments.

title: DNB starts compensation payouts to customers of Amsterdam Trade Bank
snippet: From today, savers at Amsterdam Trade Bank (ATB) can get their savings back, up to €100,000 per person. This means most account holders will regain access to their savings within a few business days.

title: Dutch pension funds’ financial position improved
snippet: In the first quarter of 2022, Dutch pension funds saw their financial position improve for the eighth consecutive quarter, as the value of their liabilities showed a steeper decline than their assets.

title: DNB activates deposit guarantee scheme for Amsterdam Trade Bank N.V. customers
snippet: On 22 April 2022, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) decided to activate the Dutch deposit guarantee scheme (DGS) for account holders of Amsterdam Trade Bank N.V. (ATB). DNB administers the Dutch Deposit Guarantee on behalf of the Dutch government.

title: Update on Amsterdam Trade Bank
snippet: The public and the media have raised questions about service provision at Amsterdam Trade Bank (ATB). De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) is in close consultation with the institution and we expect to be able to provide further information shortly.

title: Increasing preference for contactless payments
snippet: Dutch people increasingly prefer paying contactless, using either debit cards or devices such as mobile phones, smartwatches and wearables. The use of cash slightly declined during 2021, with one in five payments being made in cash.

title: New covenant lays down agreements on proper functioning of cash
snippet: Twenty-three organisations closely involved in the Dutch payment system signed a new Cash Covenant this week. The aim of the agreements is to ensure that cash continues to function properly as a means of payment at points of sale in the face of a steady increase in electronic payments.

title: Coronavirus support has been effective, but different approach needed for the future
snippet: During the coronavirus (COVID-19) crisis, the Dutch government supported trade and industry with a comprehensive package of measures.

title: Trust at the heart of the DNB Payments Strategy
snippet: In these times of increasing digitalisation, the new Payments Strategy of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) focuses on safeguarding trust.

title: Lasting effects of the pandemic on the economy and finance
snippet: On 25 March, Klaas Knot gave a masterclass at the Treasury Fair organised by DACT (Dutch Association of Corporate Treasurers). Klaas talked about the lasting effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on our economies and on finance.

title: Dutch households’ investments grew to over EUR 180 billion in 2021
snippet: Since year-end 2018, the value of investments held by Dutch households has increased by EUR 58 billion to over EUR 185 billion at year-end 2021, according to the first publication of new DNB statistics on households’ investments. This growth was mainly driven by price gains.

title: Interview Klaas Knot with Les Echos
snippet: Interview with Klaas Knot, conducted by Guillaume Benoît and Sophie Rolland of les Echos, published on March 21, 2022. See the English and French version below.

title: Value of outstanding Dutch securitisations below that of covered bonds for the first time
snippet: At 31 December 2021, the volume of Dutch securitisations outstanding, also referred to as re-packaged loans, stood at €168 billion.

title: Introduction by the President at the press conference for DNB’s 2021 Annual Report
snippet: Let me begin by saying how satisfying it is to see you all in person again, after two years of virtual press conferences, for the presentation of our annual report. Current world affairs make that feeling of satisfaction rather relative, however.

title: The expenditure rule can contribute to credible debt reduction and countercyclical fiscal policies
snippet: European fiscal rules could become more effective if they were aimed more at public spending and less at the size of the public deficit and debt.

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - Banking in the digital age: seizing opportunities, managing risks
snippet: The topic of this event is called ‘who has power in financial markets’. This is an intriguing question. As recent events show, financial markets do not operate in isolation, in a vacuum – so to speak.

title: Financial sanctions: who does what, and who monitors this?
snippet: What should banks, insurers, trust offices and other financial institutions do now that so many sanctions have been imposed? And is this process monitored?

title: The sanctions against Russia at a glance
snippet: The European Union has imposed a range of financial sanctions against Russia in the last few days. Below is an overview of the various sanctions.

title: Latest news on sanctions against Russia
snippet: The European Union has imposed and announced various sanctions against Russia in the last few weeks. Follow the latest news on the sanctions and their impact on the financial sector, payments and the economy. We will update this page on a regular basis.

title: Five questions about SWIFT [update of 4 March]
snippet: The European Union has announced that it will disconnect Russian banks from SWIFT. What is SWIFT, who does it belong to, and what are the consequences if a country is excluded?

title: What do the sanctions against the Central Bank of Russia mean?
snippet: The European Union imposed sanctions against the Central Bank of Russia on 28 February. As a result, the Russian central bank can no longer access its assets at private institutions and central banks in the European Union.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - A global Europe to meet global financial stability challenges
snippet: In his speech at Eurofi, Klaas Knot spoke in his capacity as Chair of the Financial Stability Board about the Covid exit, digitalization and climate change.

title: Nine questions on the sanctions and the economic consequences of the war
snippet: The European Union has imposed a range of sanctions on Russia. What are financial sanctions, what are the consequences of these sanctions for the Netherlands and how does the war affect our economy? Read our answers to the main questions.

title: Navigating change in the global financial system: the role of the FSB
snippet: In his speech as FSB Chair befor the G20 Finance Ministers and Governors, Klaas Knot said we may have seen only the beginning of the changes that the pandemic, digitalization and climate change are bringing to the financial system, and our economies more widely.

title: Dutch financial institutions invest heavily in new EU bonds
snippet: Dutch investments in EU bonds are among the top three largest within the European Union (EU). The capital raised with these bonds is used to finance the European Commission's (EC) extensive COVID-19 recovery plans.

title: Carbon pricing – economic impact and preconditions
snippet: A European or Dutch carbon tax will affect the Dutch economy in almost equal measure. Our economy will actually benefit from an international tax, however.

title: DNB's history is closely intertwined with slavery: DNB starts a process of reflection
snippet: Between 1814 and 1863, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) and its former directors were involved in slavery. This emerges from by independent scholarly study conducted by Leiden University, which was published today. We deeply regret these findings.

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - Changing landscape, changing supervision: preserving financial stability in times of tech revolution
snippet: In his speech at the 6th Annual Afore Conference, Steven Maijoor spoke about the complexity of reshaping regulation and supervision in a financial sector where platforms and new technology play in increasingly important role.

title: Encourage homeowners to make their homes more sustainable
snippet: In the coming years, many new homes will have to be made more sustainable. That will not happen by itself. At present, homeowners often refrain from investing in insulation or a heat pump, for example. This is partly due to financial bottlenecks.

title: Financial sector presents roadmap to circular economy
snippet: The financial sector as a driver of the circular economy. How do we achieve this? The Circular Economy Working Group of the Sustainable Finance Platform puts forward proposals for a number of concrete actions.

title: Dutch banks: “demand for loans to enterprises increased in late 2021”
snippet: Demand for loans to enterprises increased in the second half of 2021 as firms became more willing to invest.

title: Households saved less in 2021 than in first year of the COVID-19 pandemic
snippet: In 2021, Dutch households continued to save heavily. The total balance in current and savings accounts of Dutch households increased by €33.8 billion to a total of €528.4 billion in 2021.

title: Number of counterfeit euro banknotes remains stable
snippet: A total of 26,100 counterfeit euro banknotes were withdrawn from circulation in the Netherlands in 2021, roughly the same number as in 2020. Worldwide, a total of 347,000 counterfeit euro banknotes were detected, a decrease of 25% compared to 2020.

title: Financial position of Dutch pension funds improved in fourth quarter of 2021
snippet: In the fourth quarter of 2021, Dutch pension funds saw their financial position improve for the seventh consecutive quarter, as pension assets increased by €63 billion to €1,815 billion, while the value of liabilities remained virtually unchanged at €1,588 billion.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - ‘The ability and the will to act’
snippet: Good financial supervision is not only about the ability but also about the will to act. This requires supervisors to have a clear and unambiguous mandate, operational independence coupled with accountability, and a relationship with industry and government that avoids regulatory capture.

title: Better insight into bitcoin's climate impact
snippet: The total carbon footprint of the bitcoin network increased by about 25% in 2020, while the number of transactions fell by 6%. This amounts to a climate impact of about 402 kg of CO2 per bitcoin transaction in 2020,

title: Banks' profits under pressure in persistently low interest rate environment
snippet: Higher interest rate levels are favourable for the banking sector. But a scenario of persistently low interest rates poses challenges.

title: FD sentiment indicator annual overview: 2021 in the rear-view mirror
snippet: The FD sentiment indicator, based on articles in Dutch financial daily Het Financieele Dagblad (FD), has partially recovered following a sharp drop at the start of the coronavirus crisis.

title: Strong economic recovery, despite resurgence of pandemic
snippet: The Dutch economy has shown a rapid and strong recovery from the coronavirus recession of 2020. GDP is expected to grow by 4.5% this year. We have prepared the forecasts for the years ahead at a time of great uncertainty.

title: EIOPA publishes results of stress test for European insurers
snippet: EIOPA, the European supervisory authority for pension funds and insurers, has just published the results of a stress test conducted earlier this year among 44 European insurers.

title: Financial institutions share roadmap to protect biodiversity
snippet: The Biodiversity Working Group of the Sustainable Finance Platform has developed a roadmap to help financial institutions address biodiversity loss. The roadmap offers guidance for institutions that are new to this theme, but also for institutions that have already taken their first steps.

title: European stress test scenario has limited impact on Dutch insurers
snippet: Today, the European supervisory authority for insurers and pension funds (EIOPA) published a detailing the results of a stress test carried out among insurers in the European Union.

title: Minister of Finance sends Conservatrix Evaluation Committee report to the House of Representatives
snippet: This afternoon, the Dutch Minister of Finance sent the report of the Conservatrix Evaluation Committee to the House of Representatives of the Netherlands.

title: Most pension funds have started preparing for the new pension system
snippet: Some 85% of pension funds have started to prepare for the new pension system.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “On payment trends: opportunities and risks”
snippet: On 9 December, Klaas Knot spoke at the 13th Conference on Payments and Market Infrastructure, jointly organised by the National Bank of North Macedonia and De Nederlandsche Bank.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Planning is everything: the FSB’s Key Attributes and what we have learnt from them”
snippet: Speech by Klaas Knot at the FSB/FSI high-level Round Table to mark the 10th year anniversary of the adoption of the Key Attributes of Effective Resolution

title: Sustainability risks can be measured despite data constraints
snippet: The lack of consistent and reliable data makes measuring sustainability risks difficult, but not impossible.

title: Klaas Knot takes office as FSB Chair
snippet: Klaas Knot, President of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), today has taken office as Financial Stability Board (FSB) Chair. He has been serving as FSB Vice Chair before taking office.

title: Stable distribution of labour and profit income despite coronavirus crisis
snippet: Despite the coronavirus crisis, the distribution of labour and profit income has remained constant. This is reflected in the labour income share (LIS) development of the market sector in 2020. It is notable that the LIS has remained stable.

title: DNB calls for unambiguous communication about cash acceptance
snippet: Consumers are increasingly paying electronically for in-store purchases. In 3% of stores they have no alternative because the retailer pursues a card-only policy. 27% of retailers use promotional materials to encourage consumers to pay electronically.

title: The surge in euro area inflation during the pandemic: transitory but with upside risks
snippet: After being subdued for a number of years, euro area inflation has recently increased markedly. This raises two main questions. What are the drivers of this development?

title: Institutional investors increasingly investing in SPACs
snippet: Dutch investments in SPACs have increased strongly in the last year, particularly Institutional investors’ investments in these companies.

title: Remarks Klaas Knot - The outlook for inflation and monetary policy in the Euro Area
snippet: At the UBS European Conference today, Klaas Knot spoke about the outlook for inflation and monetary policy in the Euro Area.

title: New mortgage loans mainly provided by institutional investors
snippet: Dutch mortgage debt is also on the rise. Unlike before, it is mainly institutional investors who are responsible for this growth, rather than the banks. In addition, growth is relatively subdued from a historical perspective in relation to the rise in house prices.

title: Speech Olaf Sleijpen - “About failing small in order not to fail big”
snippet: On 5 November, Olaf Sleijpen opened the 24th Annual Research Conference of De Nederlandsche Bank. This year’s conference theme was: “The Economy in Transition: Efficient and Sustainable Policies to Support Business Dynamism”.

title: Supply bottlenecks visible in inflation
snippet: The higher prices that businesses have faced in recent months are increasingly translated into higher consumer prices. This mainly concerns price increases for products that previously exerted downward pressure on inflation in the Netherlands.

title: DNB publishes Pledge COP26
snippet: On 3 November 2021, on Finance Day at the COP26, we will publish a statement in which we pledge, within our mandate, to contribute to a decisive policy commitment to implement the Paris Agreement and to mitigate the impact of climate change.

title: Towards a global price for carbon emissions
snippet: From an economic perspective, pricing is the most efficient means of reducing carbon emissions. As climate change is a worldwide problem, carbon pricing works best with a global price for carbon emissions. However, complete global pricing seems infeasible.

title: Dutch businesses’ creditworthiness: so far, so good
snippet: Banks have not generally lowered their credit assessments of Dutch businesses compared to before the coronavirus crisis. In most of the hardest-hit sectors, non-performing loans have however increased markedly following the outbreak of the pandemic.

title: Financial position of Dutch pension funds improved in third quarter of 2021
snippet: In the third quarter of 2021, Dutch pension funds saw their financial position improve for the sixth consecutive quarter, as growth in their aggregate pension assets outstripped the increase in liabilities.

title: Speech Olaf Sleijpen - “The long run: the road to net zero and the role of central banks”
snippet: In his speech at the Green Economy Conference at the Bank of Lithuania today, Olaf Sleijpen argued that central bank involvement in the race to net zero is both obvious and necessary, given that climate change and other forms of environmental degradation form a major financial stability risk.

title: Safe payments are fundamental to sustaining trust and confidence in the payment system
snippet: A wide range of factors contribute to confidence in the payment system, the most important of which is being able to pay safely. High public confidence in the payment system held up well during these turbulent times.

title: Four key elements for achieving a more balanced housing market
snippet: The overheated Dutch housing market has to contend with multifaceted and urgent issues.

title: Robust economic recovery, but vulnerabilities on the rise
snippet: The economic recovery continues at a robust pace, the search for yield continues and house prices keep going up. Against this backdrop, it is important not to lose sight of growing vulnerabilities and risks to financial stability.

title: Introduction to the press conference
snippet: On 11 October 2021 Klaas Knot presented our six-monthly Financial Stabilty Report. You can read his introductory remarks here.

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “Big tech and financials: a happy marriage?”
snippet: At the BIS Conference on Regulating Big Tech, Klaas Knot said that regulators need to re-examine their regulatory framework to respond to big tech risks to financial stability and competition.

title: SER advisory report represents important step in future-proofing Dutch labour market
snippet: The draft advisory report on social and economic policy for 2021-2025 of the Economic and Social Council of the Netherlands (SER) provides valuable guidance for the incoming government, in particular for curbing the excessive flexibility in the labour market.

title: Return on Dutch investment funds is the highest in the euro area
snippet: The return on Dutch investment funds averaged 7.3% per year over the period from 2015 to July 2021.

title: ECB includes climate change in monetary policy strategy

title: ECB to revise analytical framework for monetary decision-making
snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) has decided to revise and broaden its analyses for monetary decisions. Within the new analytical framework, economic and monetary analyses will be more closely integrated, and more attention will be devoted to long-term developments and financial stability.

title: Home ownership costs to be incorporated in the inflation measure
snippet: The costs of home ownership are to be included in the inflation measure of the European Central Bank (ECB).

title: ECB sets clear and simple inflation target
snippet: Under the new strategy adopted this summer, the European Central Bank (ECB) wants to put an end to the confusion surrounding its inflation target. The ECB has raised its inflation target to 2% from the previous ‘below, but close to, 2%’.

title: Interview Klaas Knot with Bloomberg
snippet: Full quotes of the interview with Klaas Knot, conducted by Carolynn Look and Marton Eder on August 30 2021.

title: Improved European carbon pricing has limited impact on competitiveness
snippet: Implementing an EU-wide tax of €50 per tonne of carbon emitted for the manufacturing, energy and transport sectors will have a modest impact on the competitiveness of the Netherlands and most other EU Member States.

title: Households expect not to spend the vast majority of savings accumulated during the pandemic period on consumption
snippet: Due to the coronavirus measures, households have been saving more, but they only expect to use a mere 14% of these savings for consumption.

title: DNB warns against Binance
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) announces that Binance* is providing crypto services in the Netherlands without the required legal registration with DNB.

title: Dutch banking system prepared for implementation of Final Basel III Accord
snippet: In recent years, Dutch banks have strengthened their capital buffers. Four years ago, the largest Dutch banks were expected to need additional capital to meet the minimum standards set out in the Basel Accord.

title: Four questions about unregistered crypto service providers
snippet: Crypto service providers not registered with DNB are not allowed to provide their services in the Netherlands. Four questions about unregistered providers and our supervision.

title: Composition of collateral explains divergent rates in European money market
snippet: During the coronavirus (COVID-19) crisis, interest rates in the European money market were very divergent for some time. However, this was not the result of fragmentation in the market, and concerns about an impairment of monetary transmission were unjustified.

title: Dutch economy expected to bounce back swiftly after COVID-19 crisis
snippet: Following a historical contraction in gross domestic product (GDP) in 2020, the Dutch economy should recover strongly and rapidly, starting in the second quarter of 2021. snippet: As a result of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have seen their turnover drop.
